attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Will' with 'eventually' is an unhedged forecast with no deadline. Tying the deaths to AI failing to follow rules matches the paragraph just before it. Scope covers agents and, by extension, generative AI.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: one documented death after publication, causally linked to an AI rule or guardrail failure, would count. It correctly says that time passing without such a death cannot contradict an open-ended 'eventually'.

evidence.note: News report on the Acton killings after publication. It covers prosecutors' claims of ChatGPT use only. It shows no guardrail failure and no causal link; the case is still being investigated and a not-guilty plea was entered.
Anthropic's own disclosure of agent actions that broke instructions, with minimal real-world impact. It shows rule-following failures but no deaths.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The packet has no documented death after publication that is credibly tied to an AI agent's rule or guardrail failure, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The Acton case is an allegation of chatbot use, with no established failure or causation. A lack of qualifying deaths so far cannot contradict 'eventually'.
